questions.question: Non-polio enterovirus.

parts.text: What are two types of non-enterovirus that were recently identified as causes of acute flaccid paralysis?
Other than neurologic disease, what are six ways that non-polio enterovirus can present?

parts_raw.text: What are two types of non-enterovirus that were recently identified as causes of acute flaccid paralysis
Other than neurologic disease, what are 6 ways that non polio enterovirus can present

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Fecal-oral. (2) Respiratory/oral (droplet) spread. b) Typically 3-6 days (range ~2-10 days). c) The part asks for non-enterovirus causes of AFP recently identified: (1) West Nile virus. (2) Acute flaccid myelitis has also been linked to other flaviviruses (e.g. Japanese encephalitis); note the classic recently-recognised enteroviral causes are EV-D68 and EV-A71. d) (1) Hand-foot-and-mouth disease. (2) Herpangina. (3) Myopericarditis. (4) Epidemic pleurodynia. (5) Acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis. (6) Nonspecific febrile illness with exanthem/respiratory infection.

questions.question: Enterovirus infection.
questions.question_raw: Enterovirus. What is the incubation period. Two enteroviruses that cause acute flaccid paralysis (non-polio). 6 non-neurologic presentations of enterovirus.

parts.text: Two enteroviruses that cause acute flaccid paralysis (non-polio).

parts_raw.text: b. Two enteroviruses that cause acute flaccid paralysis (non-polio).

questions.model_answer:
a) The typical incubation period for non-polio enterovirus infection is about 3 to 6 days.
b) (1) Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71). (2) Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68).
c) (1) Hand-foot-and-mouth disease. (2) Herpangina. (3) Pleurodynia (Bornholm disease). (4) Myopericarditis. (5) Acute respiratory disease (e.g., EV-D68 bronchiolitis/pneumonia). (6) Acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis (EV-D70, CV-A24).
questions.beyond_mandell: The incubation period is not stated in this chapter slice; the 3-6 day range is standard Mandell/CDC teaching for non-polio enteroviruses.

cohort_answer.text: a) 3-5 days. b) Enterovirus A71; Enterovirus D68. c) Respiratory disease; hand, foot and mouth disease; herpangina; pleurodynia; myopericarditis; ocular infections.
